# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-2 (Extended v47)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion and Bombarda's restaurant); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; Valjean enters courtroom; WITNESSES TESTIFY; Valjean rises and reveals himself; DEPARTS COURTROOM; ARRIVES AT INFIRMARY NEXT MORNING AT DAYBREAK; CHAMPMATHIEU ACQUITTED; ARREST ORDER ISSUED; JAVERT ARRIVES AT INFIRMARY ANTECHAMBER; JAVERT ENTERS FANTINE'S ROOM WITH SOLDIERS; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED)**; 1862 (narrative reflection); present day (spring to late August/early September, England); future wedding (following spring); 1795 (Valjean's theft and trial)
- Primary locations: M. sur M., Montfermeil, Arras (Hotel de la Poste, Court of Assizes in Prefecture, council-chamber, courtroom with corridors, steps, gratings, door, audience hall); infirmary (laboratory, Fantine's chamber, Hall of Assizes corridor); England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby)
- **Journey and courtroom entry (completed)**: Valjean hired Scaufflaire's tilbury; departed M. sur M. night of January 1823; arrived Arras nearly eight o'clock evening; left alone in council-chamber; fled corridor in terror; re-entered courtroom despite fear; concealed face behind cardboard boxes; gradually recovered composure sufficient to listen.
- **Trial proceedings and testimony (completed)**: Champmathieu (accused) made incoherent denials; Ex-convict Brevet testified (age sixty, recognized Valjean as galley companion entered 1796 left 1815); Prisoner-for-life Chenildieu (red cassock, green cap, fifty years old, nicknamed "Je-nie Dieu"); Prisoner-for-life Cochepaille (peasant from Lourdes, brigand).
- **Valjean's courtroom revelation (completed)**: Man (Valjean) rose among spectators, pushed through half-door, stood in middle of hall; his gray hair had turned entirely white during the hour he sat in courtroom; clerk's lamp illumined countenance; audience experienced indescribable sensation; Valjean advanced towards witnesses; addressed Chenildieu directly with specific knowledge of burn mark on right shoulder and T.F.P. letters from chafing-dish coal attempt to efface them.
- **Courtroom aftermath and acquittal (completed)**: Chamber contained no longer judges, accusers, gendarmes; only staring eyes and sympathizing hearts; no question put, no authority intervened; all felt inwardly dazzled; Valjean departed courtroom with divine something causing crowd to part; district-attorney, recovering from shock, deplored "mad deed" but found sentiments of public, court, and jury against him; counsel for defence established Champmathieu innocent in light of Valjean's revelations; President summed up in favour of acquittal; jury freed Champmathieu within minutes.
- **Legal response and arrest order (completed)**: After Champmathieu's liberation, district-attorney and President conferred "as to the necessity of seizing the person of M. le Maire of M. sur M."; President did not object strongly; order of arrest signed by district-attorney: "Inspector Javert will apprehend the body of the Sieur Madeleine, mayor of M. sur M., who, in this day's session of the court, was recognized as the liberated convict, Jean Valjean."
- **Valjean's return to infirmary (completed)**: Half-hour after midnight: Valjean quit Hall of Assizes; regained inn; engaged place in mail-wagon; arrived M. sur M. little before six o'clock morning; posted letter to M. Laffitte; entered infirmary to see Fantine.
- **Javert's arrival at infirmary (completed)**: Messenger informed Javert of Arras events; Javert penetrated antechamber of infirmary; appeared outwardly cool, calm, grave, gray hair smooth; but buckle of leather stock under left ear instead of nape indicated unwonted agitation; made simple requisition on neighboring post for corporal and four soldiers; left soldiers in courtyard; had portress point out Fantine's room; portress unsuspicious, accustomed to armed men inquiring for mayor.

## Javert's Psychological State at Arrest
- **Triumph and vindication**: Satisfaction of finally seizing Jean Valjean caused all in his soul to appear in countenance. Humiliation of losing scent and erring regarding Champmathieu was effaced by pride in having divined correctly initially and cherished just instinct for five years.
- **Metaphysical exaltation**: Without clearly conceptualizing it, Javert felt confused intuition of necessity of his presence and success; he personified justice, light, truth in their celestial function of crushing evil; behind and around him at infinite distance: authority, reason, case judged, legal conscience, public prosecution, all the stars; he was protecting order, causing law to yield thunders, avenging society, lending hand to absolute; erect in midst of glory.
- **Pathological grandeur and fanatic virtue**: Remnant of defiance and combat in victory; erect, haughty, brilliant; flaunted superhuman bestiality of ferocious archangel; terrible shadow of action made vague flash of social sword visible in clenched fist; happy and indignant, held heel upon crime, vice, rebellion, perdition, hell; radiant, exterminating, smiling; incontestable grandeur in monstrous Saint Michael.
- **Narrative assessment**: Probity, sincerity, candor, conviction, sense of duty become hideous when wrongly directed but remain grand; majesty of human conscience clings to them in midst of horror; virtues with one vice—error; honest, pitiless joy of fanatic in full flood of atrocity preserves lugubriously venerable radiance; Javert in formidable happiness was to be pitied as every ignorant man who triumphs; nothing so poignant and terrible as this face displaying evil of the good.

## Fantine's Death (Completed)
- **Recognition and terror**: Had not seen Javert since day mayor tore her from man; ailing brain comprehended nothing but that he had come to get her; could not endure terrible face; felt life quitting her; hid face in both hands; shrieked in anguish.
- **Physical collapse and final moments**: Raised herself in bed with bound, supporting on stiffened arms and both hands; gazed at Valjean, gazed at Javert, gazed at nun; opened mouth as though to speak; rattle from depths of throat; teeth chattered; stretched out arms in agony, opening hands convulsively, fumbling like drowning person; then suddenly fell back on pillow; became motionless body.
- **Valjean's farewell**: Stepped to old iron bedstead in corner of room; wrenched off head-piece (already dilapidated); grasped principal rod like bludgeon; glanced at Javert; Javert retreated towards door; Valjean armed with bar of iron walked slowly up to Fantine's couch; turned and said to Javert in barely audible voice (words not recorded); then rested elbow on knob at head of bed, brow on hand; began contemplating motionless body of Fantine extended there; remained mute, absorbed, with no further thought of anything connected with this life; nothing but inexpressible pity on face and attitude; bent towards Fantine, spoke to her in low voice (words not heard by anyone on earth).
- **Mystical attestation**: Sister Simplice, sole witness, often said that at moment Valjean whispered in Fantine's ear, she distinctly beheld ineffable smile dawn on pale lips and in dim eyes filled with amazement of tomb.

## Main Characters and Relationships

**Jean Valjean / M. Madeleine—IDENTITY REVEALED, ARRESTED AT FANTINE'S DEATHBED**
- Rose in courtroom to reveal himself; hair turned white during hour of trial; allowed innocent man to be freed; arrived M. sur M. little before six o'clock morning; entered infirmary; present beside dying Fantine; confronted Javert with iron bar wrenched from bedstead; spoke final words to Fantine in low voice; arrested.

**Fantine—DEAD (January 1823, infirmary)**
- Terminal illness advanced; had gray hair (two-month change from first visit); spent sleepless feverish night of happy visions; had fantasized future life with Cosette; suddenly experienced alarming vision (death manifestation); recognized Javert; experienced terror; raised herself in final agony; fell back motionless; received Valjean's whispered farewell; Sister Simplice witnessed ineffable smile dawn on pale lips and in dim eyes filled with amazement of tomb at moment of her passing.

**Javert (Police Inspector, M. sur M.)—ARREST EXECUTED**
- Received arrest order: "Inspector Javert will apprehend the body of the Sieur Madeleine, mayor of M. sur M., who, in this day's session of the court, was recognized as the liberated convict, Jean Valjean"; made simple requisition for corporal and four soldiers; left soldiers in courtyard; had portress point out Fantine's room; did not proceed according to custom, did not exhibit warrant of arrest; viewed Valjean as mysterious combatant he had grasped for five years without throwing; arrest was not beginning but end; confined himself to saying "Be quick about it!"; retreated towards door when Valjean armed himself with iron bar; executed arrest of Valjean.

**Cosette** (Age ~7-8 in 1823)
- At Montfermeil with Thénardiers; subject of Fantine's final maternal longing and deathbed expectations.

**Thénardier** (Cook-shop keeper, Montfermeil)
- Continues obstruction of Cosette's departure.

**Sister Simplice** (Infirmary nun)
- Sole witness to Valjean's final whispered words to Fantine; testified throughout life that she witnessed ineffable smile dawn on Fantine's pale lips at moment of death; observed Valjean's inexpressible pity and meditation beside dying woman.

**Courtroom Witnesses and Officials** (Trial completed)
- Brevet, Chenildieu, Cochepaille, Champmathieu (acquitted), President, District-attorney (drafted arrest order).

**Minor Characters**
- **Ludrek Prydenridge**: head of Prydenridge household; owns ivory chalice (function unclear, possibly anachronistic or out-of-place detail); **claim/rumor**: Only Luvie Prydenridge knew old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar (unconnected to main narrative).
- **Portress** (Infirmary): unsuspicious; pointed out Fantine's room to Javert; accustomed to armed men inquiring for mayor.
- **M. Laffitte**: recipient of letter posted by Valjean upon returning to M. sur M.

## Social Aftermath
- **Town's response to arrest (January 1823)**: Arrest of M. Madeleine occasioned extraordinary commotion in M. sur M.; at single word "He was a convict," nearly every one deserted him; in less than two hours all good he had done forgotten; he was nothing but "convict from galleys"; details of Arras proceedings not yet known; all day conversations of denunciation and betrayal heard throughout town.

## Themes
- **Redemptive sacrifice completed, legal consequence executed, maternal transcendence achieved**: Valjean revealed himself, saved innocent man, returned to Fantine's side, spoke final words of love/farewell, was arrested; Fantine died with mystical smile witnessing ineffable grace; both achieved transcendence through self-sacrifice and surrender.
- **Javert's pathological virtue and fanatic justice**: Javert's triumph illuminates evil of the good—probity, sincerity, conviction wrongly directed become hideous yet remain grand; he viewed himself as celestial instrument crushing evil; ignorant man triumphing in formidable happiness deserving pity; nothing so terrible as this face displaying majesty of human conscience corrupted by error.
- **Hair-whitening and temporal collapse**: Valjean's gray hair turned white in single hour; Fantine's turned gray over two months; physical transformations mark spiritual transformations; both achieved liminal transcendence at moment of ultimate trial.
- **Maternal redemption and ineffable grace**: Fantine's final moments marked by ineffable smile witnessed by Sister Simplice; Valjean's whispered words to dying Fantine suggested forgiveness, love, transcendent communication; ineffable smile on pale lips filled with amazement of tomb indicated vision or grace beyond earthly comprehension.
- **Justice apparatus overwhelming sentiment with legal machinery**: Despite public and court sympathy, district-attorney and President moved swiftly to arrest; legal machinery reasserted itself; Javert executed arrest coolly while Fantine died and Valjean surrendered.
